subject: Some questions about the application process

messages.author: 406ca2cd457f303c
messages.subject: Some questions about the application process
parts:
Hello everyone. I'm R applicant Matthieu Lestel from France. I would like to work on the Additional performance measures and attribution functionality to PerformanceAnalytics and PortfolioAnalytics project for the gsoc this year. However as it's my first year in this program  and I have some questions about the application process.

For the Short description area, should I use the one in project ideas website or do it myself. And how accurate is it supposed to be ? Am I supposed to explain every task I am to do during the programm here ?

Then I have a few questions about the R template.

- I don't understand what the link_id field is
- In the main step field, is it here I am to explain everything I would do during the summer ?
- Is the timeline field designed to estimate the time I will need for every task ?

Then I made a small Rscript demo to explain the use of the package PerformanceAnalytics but I don't know where I should include it in the application process. At the moment I have only made a git repository on GitHub.

Last question : is it possible to modify his application when submitted on google-melange or is it better to discuss the content of the different fields with the mentors before submitting the application ?

It's a bit long and I'm sorry the answer are not already given somewhere but I couldn't find them in the FAQ nor in the R website.

Thank you in advance for your answers.

Matthieu

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: Some questions about the application process
parts:
On Mon, 2012-04-02 at 09:14 -0700, Matthieu Lestel wrote:
> Hello everyone. I'm R applicant Matthieu Lestel from France. I would
> like to work on the Additional performance measures and attribution
> functionality to PerformanceAnalytics and PortfolioAnalytics project
> for the gsoc this year. However as it's my first year in this program
> and I have some questions about the application process.
>
> For the Short description area, should I use the one in project ideas
> website or do it myself. And how accurate is it supposed to be ?

The short description could easily be the one from the project idea
page.

> Am I supposed to explain every task I am to do during the programm
> here ?
>

> Then I have a few questions about the R template.
>
> - I don't understand what the link_id field is

The melange user id, for you and for the mentors.

mine is 'braverock'

> - In the main step field, is it here I am to explain everything I
> would do during the summer ?

I do suggest adding a few paragraphs here describing your general
approach, as well as the main chunks of work.

> - Is the timeline field designed to estimate the time I will need for
> every task ?
>

The timeline should cover all the major steps you need in your
development, and should have some slack for scope changes. The major
goal here is to communicate to everyone that your approach is credible.

> Then I made a small Rscript demo to explain the use of the package
> PerformanceAnalytics but I don't know where I should include it in the
> application process. At the moment I have only made a git repository
> on GitHub.

You can either add it to the applciation, or just send the 'test'
demonstration to the mentors. You've already sent it to Peter and I, so
you don't need to put it in the application.

> Last question : is it possible to modify his application when
> submitted on google-melange or is it better to discuss the content of
> the different fields with the mentors before submitting the
> application ?
>

You can modify the application up until the Apr 6th 19:00 UTC deadline,
which is 4 days and 2 hours from now as I write this.

Once your application is posted, other R mentors may also comment on the
application. I suggest that you respond to these mentor comments as
quickly as possible, to refine your approach and communication.

> It's a bit long and I'm sorry the answer are not already given
> somewhere but I couldn't find them in the FAQ nor in the R website.
> Thank you in advance for your answers.

Regards,

- Brian
